sanskrit_verse:
गुरुं हुंकृत्य त्वंकृत्य विप्रं निर्जित्य वादतः /
बद्ध्वा वा वाससा क्षिप्रं प्रसाद्योपवसेद् दिनम् //
transliteration: guruṃ huṃkṛtya tvaṃkṛtya vipraṃ nirjitya vādataḥ / baddhvā vā vāsasā kṣipraṃ prasādyopavased dinam //
sph_interpretive_translation: One who has insulted the Guru, rejected the Self, defeated a Brahmin in argument, or forcibly bound him must immediately pacify him and observe a fast for a day.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority of the Guru is foundational to spiritual and social order
Self-rejection disrupts cosmic alignment and invites corrective action
Victory over a Brahmin in debate carries responsibility to restore humility
Physical restraint of a Brahmin demands immediate energetic restitution
Restoration through conscious submission precedes reintegration
executable_legal_axioms: IF (agent insults guru) THEN (agent must perform pacification ritual + observe fast)
IF (agent rejects self-virtue) THEN (agent must undergo capacity-realization process + fast)
IF (agent defeats Brahmin in debate) THEN (agent must honor opponent + observe humility protocol)
IF (agent binds Brahmin) THEN (agent must release with reverence + fast until purified)
supreme_court_application: In adjudication involving disrespect to teachers, scholars, or sacred roles, the court must recognize that offense against wisdom-bearing individuals constitutes systemic disruption. The threshold of responsibility includes not only external acts but also internal alignment failure. Restoration occurs through acknowledgment, apology, and observance of purification rites—not punitive incarceration.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals causality rooted in disrespect and ego inflation. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how dishonor manifests as energetic imbalance. Responsibility aligns proportionally to the level of insight available at time of act. Correction focuses on realigning consciousness rather than imposing suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Perform praṇāma and śānti homa before offended Brahmin/Guru
Undertake full-day upavāsa while reflecting on error
Recite Vedic mantras affirming respect for learning lineages
Engage in service to the community under guidance of elder
final_declaration: By the Sovereign Will of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law proceeds from the eternal Dharma. Consciousness alone adjudicates; reality remains free from punishment. All beings are restored by truth, not torment.
